comparison: Strong agreement on core methodological contribution (C5-C8, C14, C20, C67-C68). Both evaluations find the approach mathematically principled and empirically validated. OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment while peer review emphasizes overall compelling evidence and importance to the field.

Perfect claim overlap (C37, C71) on Riemannian geometry findings. Both evaluations support the claims about tangent space embedding benefits. OpenEval provides statistical detail (p=0.0313), while peer review accepts implicitly through overall positive assessment without specific critique.

Strong agreement on reliability assessment (C43-C50, C70). Both accept the 0% risk finding for linear Fisher kernel and robustness comparisons. OpenEval provides quantitative detail while peer review explicitly acknowledges 'lower variance on many individual traits.'

Agreement on train-test separation findings (C63-C64, C66, C80). Both accept the real data results and simulation-revealed limitations. OpenEval provides detailed explanation of the principled limitation, while peer review accepts implicitly through positive assessment of 'out of sample assessment.'

Agreement on supplementary robustness analyses (C39-C40, C75). Both accept findings about persistence of advantages across data configurations. OpenEval treats as strengthening main results, peer review accepts implicitly without specific critique.

Agreement on simulation findings about state parameters vs transitions (C51-C57). Both accept perfect recovery of state differences and poor recovery of transitions. Peer reviewer explicitly notes 'HMM state matrix may be more informative' while OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment.

Agreement on feature importance analysis from real data (C58-C62, C78). Both accept that state parameters drive predictions. Peer review summary directly references this finding, OpenEval emphasizes consistency across simulation and real data.

Perfect claim overlap (C76-C77) on Gaussian kernel findings. Both accept that Gaussian kernels are less reliable and computationally expensive. OpenEval provides detailed justification, peer review accepts implicitly as methodological detail.

Perfect claim overlap (C42) on variable-specific predictability. Both treat as descriptive finding. OpenEval notes it provides context, peer review references 'many individual traits' indicating acceptance.

Disagreement on interpretation of accuracy comparisons (C21-C22, C28-C29, C34, C69). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting only 2 of many comparisons reached significance and claims are overstated. Peer review rates SUPPORTED, accepting 'higher prediction accuracy' without challenging statistical nuances.

Partial overlap on statistical comparisons (C28-C29, C34, C69). Both acknowledge the results, but OpenEval emphasizes honest assessment of limited significance while peer review focuses on overall acceptance of comparative findings without detailed statistical critique.
Partial overlap on supplementary analysis (C41). Both support the finding. OpenEval treats as robustness check strengthening main results, peer review accepts implicitly without specific discussion.
